title: Civil Writ Back / Endorsement — Thomas Smith v. James M. Wrenn (reverse side of warrant)
text:
[Written on outside/back of folded document, rotated — address panel:]
Thomas Smith
vs.
James M. Wrenn
Copy of Petition
Copy of Notice[?]

[Body of document — written upside-down/reverse, transcribed right-reading:]
State of Missouri }
County of Cedar   }  A. H. McCannaway[?]

1867
[Stockton?] Mo 14th day of January
Before me[?] a Justice[?] or officer in and of the said
affixed my name and seal of the said
hath subscribed my name[?]
and cause[?] the testimony inscribed above
is correct[?]. Now here for my office I[?]
on return* the copy of the aforesd[?] justice
in case[?] can certify that the Circuit Court
Now Grantordin[?] Yr[?] for said case to be finally settled
of Missouri the Clk[?] Custnery[?] clerk to make[?] the use
[remaining lines heavily faded and illegible]
Circuit Court of County A. (Cedar) [?]
A. H. McCannaway
State of Missouri
County of Cedar
A. H. McCannaway
Clerk of Circuit Court, [Cedar] Missouri
notes: This is the reverse/back side of the folded Wrenn warrant document. The outside panel shows the address endorsement: 'Thomas Smith vs. James M. Wrenn / Copy of Petition / Copy of Notice[?]'. The internal text is written in a different orientation and is heavily faded and largely illegible. What is legible appears to be a certification or return by the clerk A. H. McCannaway (same person as Q. H. Cannaway on the front — possibly initials misread). Much of the body text is [illegible] due to fading and the reversed/folded nature of the document.
